turns.learner: Hello teacher. I want to practise talking about things around me, like my room and my house.
turns.tutor:
Hello! Good plan. Your room has many things, like a bed or a chair.

We use a the first time we talk about a thing. Then we use the for the same thing.

Example: I have a bag. The bag is blue.

Your turn: write two short sentences about one thing in your room.

turns.learner: I have a lamp. A lamp is big and white.
turns.tutor:
You have most of it. "I have a lamp." is a good first sentence.

Let us sharpen one part. Look at the first word in your second sentence: "A lamp is big and white."

Is it the same lamp, or a new lamp? Look again and write that sentence one more time.

turns.learner: It is the same lamp. I write again: A lamp is big and white. Is it wrong?
turns.tutor:
You are right: it is the same lamp. That is the important part.

I want to know your idea. You wrote "a" before lamp in both sentences. Why did you choose that word? Tell me in one short word or phrase.

turns.learner: Because lamp is one thing. We say a for one thing, I think.
turns.tutor:
You are right: "a" is for one thing. But it is not the word for the same lamp the second time.

Look at the first word in "A lamp is big and white." Think: you already know this lamp.

Write the second sentence again with a different first word.

turns.learner: Maybe: My lamp is big and white? I am not sure about this word.
turns.tutor:
"My lamp is big and white." is a good sentence. You changed the first word, and that is the right part to look at.

The lesson word is a, an or the. Which word do you choose here? Write one word.

turns.learner: I think a. Because one lamp.
turns.tutor:
"One lamp" is true, and "a" fits one thing. But it is not the word for the same lamp after the first sentence.

Look at my example: "I have a bag. The bag is blue." Look at the first word before each "bag".

Which word is different?
